content.text: /ext:medcp Which antidepressant classes are most commonly used in older adults (³65)?
I'll query the EHR database to find antidepressant prescribing patterns in older adults. Let me first look at the available tables.

This is an OMOP CDM database. Antidepressant classes are captured in the OMOP vocabulary via ATC classification (ATC N06A). I'll identify antidepressant classes through the `concept_ancestor` hierarchy, then count patients aged ≥65 with exposures, grouped by ATC 4th-level class (SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, etc.).

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT concept_id, concept_name, concept_code, concept_class_id, vocabulary_id
FROM omop.concept
WHERE vocabulary_id = 'ATC'
  AND concept_code IN ('N06A','N06AA','N06AB','N06AF','N06AG','N06AX')
ORDER BY concept_code;

The ATC 4th-level classes are the standard way to group antidepressants. Now I'll count distinct patients aged ≥65 with at least one exposure to a drug under each class, using `concept_ancestor` to map ingredient/drug concepts up to the ATC class.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT anc.concept_name AS drug_class,
       anc.concept_code AS atc_code,
       COUNT(DISTINCT de.person_id) AS n_patients,
       COUNT(*) AS n_exposures
FROM omop.drug_exposure de
JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = de.person_id
JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
JOIN omop.concept anc ON anc.concept_id = ca.ancestor_concept_id
WHERE anc.vocabulary_id = 'ATC'
  AND anc.concept_class_id = 'ATC 4th'
  AND anc.concept_code LIKE 'N06A%'
  AND (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM de.drug_exposure_start_date) - p.year_of_birth) >= 65
GROUP BY anc.concept_name, anc.concept_code
ORDER BY n_patients DESC;

content.text: The full join over `drug_exposure × concept_ancestor` timed out. I'll narrow it: pre-aggregate distinct patients per drug concept first (with the age filter), then map to ATC classes — this shrinks the ancestor join dramatically.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH exp AS (
  SELECT de.drug_concept_id, COUNT(DISTINCT de.person_id) AS n_patients
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de
  JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = de.person_id
  WHERE (YEAR(de.drug_exposure_start_date) - p.year_of_birth) >= 65
    AND de.drug_concept_id IN (
      SELECT ca.descendant_concept_id
      FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca
      JOIN omop.concept anc ON anc.concept_id = ca.ancestor_concept_id
      WHERE anc.vocabulary_id = 'ATC' AND anc.concept_code = 'N06A'
    )
  GROUP BY de.drug_concept_id
)
SELECT anc.concept_name AS drug_class, anc.concept_code AS atc_code,
       SUM(exp.n_patients) AS patient_exposure_sum
FROM exp
JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = exp.drug_concept_id
JOIN omop.concept anc ON anc.concept_id = ca.ancestor_concept_id
WHERE anc.vocabulary_id = 'ATC' AND anc.concept_class_id = 'ATC 4th'
  AND anc.concept_code LIKE 'N06A%'
GROUP BY anc.concept_name, anc.concept_code
ORDER BY patient_exposure_sum DESC;

The failures tell me the `concept_ancestor` join is the bottleneck — antidepressants have thousands of descendant drug/dose concepts, and joining that fan-out against the full `drug_exposure` table exceeds the 600s deadline even after pre-aggregation. My assumption that I could resolve classes at query time via the ATC hierarchy is too expensive for this backend.

Better approach: aggregate at the **ingredient** level instead. `drug_era` is already collapsed to ingredient concepts (far smaller than `drug_exposure`), and each antidepressant ingredient maps cleanly to one class. I'll get patient counts per ingredient among ≥65s, then group into classes myself.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT c.concept_name AS ingredient,
       COUNT(DISTINCT dre.person_id) AS n_patients
FROM omop.drug_era dre
JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = dre.person_id
JOIN omop.concept c ON c.concept_id = dre.drug_concept_id
WHERE (YEAR(dre.drug_era_start_date) - p.year_of_birth) >= 65
  AND dre.drug_concept_id IN (
    SELECT ca.descendant_concept_id
    FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca
    JOIN omop.concept anc ON anc.concept_id = ca.ancestor_concept_id
    WHERE anc.vocabulary_id = 'ATC' AND anc.concept_code = 'N06A'
  )
  AND c.concept_class_id = 'Ingredient'
GROUP BY c.concept_name
ORDER BY n_patients DESC;
